Control when each supported harness may choose a Skill on its own.

Model invocation answers one question: **may the Harness choose this Skill on
its own, or must a person ask for it?**

It does not grant tools, approve commands, or decide where a Skill is
installed. Harness permissions remain the runtime authorization boundary, and
a Binding separately selects the Harness and Scope for a Projection.

## Policies

SKIT uses three portable policies:

| Policy        | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `explicit`    | The Harness should use the Skill only when a person asks for it.        |
| `implicit`    | The Harness may choose the Skill when its description matches the task. |
| `host-policy` | Do not impose a SKIT preference; let the Harness use its own behavior.  |

An author can declare a policy for a contained Skill with `invocation` in
`skit.json`. A Library Owner can override it for one Binding with
`skit enable --invocation`.

The additional CLI choice `declared` is not a fourth policy. It clears the
device-local override and follows the author's declaration. If the author did
not declare a preference, the Harness decides.

```sh
# Follow the author
skit enable owner/tools#review --for codex --invocation declared

# Override this Binding on this device
skit enable owner/tools#review --for codex --invocation explicit

# Return control to the Harness
skit enable owner/tools#review --for codex --invocation host-policy
```

## Harness behavior

Harnesses do not share one invocation field. SKIT translates the effective
policy into metadata understood by each Harness when it materializes the
Projection.

“Supported” means SKIT can represent the policy in that Harness's native
Skill metadata. It does not mean the Harness will execute a Skill without its
ordinary permission checks.

### Claude Code

**Supported.** Claude Code stores the policy in `SKILL.md`.

- `explicit` sets `disable-model-invocation: true`.
- `implicit` sets `disable-model-invocation: false`.
- `host-policy` removes SKIT's constraint.

Explicit invocation remains available when model invocation is disabled.

### Codex

**Supported.** Codex stores the policy in `agents/openai.yaml`, not in
`SKILL.md`.

- `explicit` sets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`.
- `implicit` sets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: true`.
- `host-policy` removes SKIT's constraint.

SKIT preserves unrelated Codex metadata.

### Devin

**Supported.** Devin stores permitted invokers in the `triggers` field in
`SKILL.md`.

- `explicit` sets `triggers: [user]`.
- `implicit` sets `triggers: [user, model]`.
- `host-policy` preserves authored triggers, or uses Devin's default.

This means SKIT does not erase an author-owned restriction when returning
control to Devin.

### OpenCode V1

**Projected, but `explicit` cannot be enforced.** OpenCode V1 ignores the V2
metadata SKIT writes.

- `explicit` sets `metadata["opencode/autoinvoke"]: "false"`, but V1 ignores it.
- `implicit` sets `metadata["opencode/autoinvoke"]: "true"`, matching V1's default.
- `host-policy` removes SKIT's constraint.

V1 advertises every permitted, described Skill to the model. Denying permission
is not an explicit-only alternative: it also prevents the Skill from loading
when requested.

### OpenCode V2

**Supported.** OpenCode V2 stores the policy in the portable `metadata` map in
`SKILL.md`.

- `explicit` sets `metadata["opencode/autoinvoke"]: "false"`.
- `implicit` sets `metadata["opencode/autoinvoke"]: "true"`.
- `host-policy` removes SKIT's constraint.

Setting `autoinvoke` to `"false"` removes the Skill from model-facing discovery
while keeping explicit activation available by Skill ID.

SKIT uses the same `opencode` Binding for both generations and does not detect
the installed generation before projection. V1 safely ignores the metadata;
V2 enforces it.

OpenCode's `slash` field is separate. It controls visibility in interactive
command catalogs; it does not control whether the model is told about the
Skill.

See the upstream [OpenCode V1 Agent Skills documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills)
and [OpenCode V2 Skills documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills).

## Author declarations and native metadata

The portable `invocation` declaration records the author's intent. Native
metadata lets the same artifact behave correctly when used without SKIT.

Inside an Author Workspace, run [`skit author invocation`](/cli/reference/commands/author-invocation)
to write declared policies into the native metadata SKIT currently supports:

```sh
skit author invocation
skit author invocation --dry-run
```

SKIT checks that an author's portable declaration agrees with required native
metadata before publication. A Library override never mutates the retained
artifact; it changes only the derived Projection for that Binding.

## Precedence

SKIT resolves invocation intent in this order:

1. The Library Owner's device-local Binding override.
2. The author's portable `invocation` declaration.
3. Native Harness metadata already present in a legacy or undeclared Skill.
4. The Harness's own default.

The CLI and TUI report both the effective policy and whether it came from the
author, a local override, or the Harness default.

## Invocation is not authorization

An implicit policy permits the Harness to consider a Skill. The Harness may
still deny or ask for approval when the Skill loads or when its instructions
lead to tool use. Conversely, an explicit policy does not grant permission to
run everything described by the Skill.

Do not use invocation policy as a security boundary. Review the Skill and
configure the Harness's permissions independently.

Use [`skit enable`](/cli/reference/commands/enable) to set a Binding policy and
[`skit disable`](/cli/reference/commands/disable) to remove the Binding.
